chunks: And from him, from Al-A'ala, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:

I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about the apostate, so he (peace be upon him) said: 'The one who desires away from Islam and disbelieves in what was revealed to Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family) after his Islam, there is no repentance for him, and his killing is obligatory, and his wife is divorced from him, and what he leaves is distributed among his children.'

key_terms.مُحَمَّدٍ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ): Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family)

ai.seo_question: What are the legal consequences of apostasy in Shia Islam regarding repentance, execution, marriage, and inheritance?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the definitive status of the apostate (murtadd) as one who rejects the core revelation, resulting in irrevocable divorce (tanfiz) and the exclusion of the apostate from inheriting from their heirs. It reflects the classical Shia juristic consensus that apostasy is a capital offense with immediate legal consequences, distinct from mere disbelief prior to conversion.
